spawnBayes

spawnBayes estimates salmon spawner abundance and run timing from repeated live-count surveys.Unlike traditional area-under-the-curve (TAUC) approaches, spawnBayes jointly estimates abundance, run timing, effective residence time, and associated uncertainty using a hierarchical Bayesian model.

The package supports analyses of individual streams as well as integrated analyses across multiple groups. Groups may represent reaches, streams, rivers, populations, index areas, or other biologically meaningful assessment units. In multi-group analyses, timing information is shared among groups while abundance is estimated separately for each group.

The package is designed to support salmon stock assessment and escapement monitoring programs. Users provide survey dates and spawner counts and obtain estimates of annual abundance, run timing, effective residence time, and associated uncertainty.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("SiRE-P/spawnBayes")

Prerequisites

spawnBayes uses cmdstanr and requires a local installation of CmdStan.

Install cmdstanr:

install.packages(
  "cmdstanr",
  repos = c(
    "https://mc-stan.org/r-packages/",
    getOption("repos")
  )
)

Then follow the official CmdStan installation guide:

https://mc-stan.org/docs/cmdstan-guide/installation.html

Verify the installation:

cmdstanr::cmdstan_version()

Data Requirements

Required columns:

Variable Description
date Survey date
spawner_counts Number of live spawners observed

Optional columns:

Variable Description
group Group identifier (reach, stream, river, population, index area, etc.)
observer_efficiency Proportion of fish detected during a survey (0-1)
coverage Proportion of spawning habitat surveyed (0-1)
survey_error_group Observation-error category used to estimate group-specific observation dispersion

If group is omitted, all observations are assumed to belong to a single group.

If observer_efficiency or coverage are omitted, values of 1 are assumed.

If survey_error_group is omitted, all observations are assumed to share a common observation-error distribution.

What Is a Group?

A group is the unit for which abundance is estimated and timing is allowed to vary independently.

Groups may represent:

  • stream reaches
  • streams
  • rivers
  • populations
  • index areas
  • other biologically meaningful assessment units

Single-group analyses estimate abundance for one group. Multi-group analyses share timing information among groups while estimating abundance separately for each group.

In general, groups should be analysed together when they are expected to share broad seasonal timing patterns and survey information from one group may help inform timing estimates in another.

Groups may be analysed separately or jointly. When in doubt, fitting both a single-group and multi-group model can help assess whether shared timing information improves inference.

Data Template

Create a template CSV file in the current working directory:

template_file()

This creates:

spawnBayes_template.csv

containing the required and optional input columns.

If you use spawnBayes in a publication, please cite:
